subject: Dedicated capacity recap & next steps — Orion Health
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@orionhealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 5 Jun 2026 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call recap — dedicated capacity needs & next steps

Hi Samantha —

Thanks again for your time today. Quick recap from our discovery so we’re aligned and can move this to procurement:  

Pain points and goals (as discussed)
- Performance: current latency tail (p95) for critical inference calls is ~260ms on your self-hosted endpoints; target is <=120ms for real-time clinician workflows.
- Isolation & compliance: PHI-sensitive workloads require network isolation and stricter auditability (SOC2 + retention controls).
- Predictable throughput: peak batch processing windows produce bursts that currently saturate GPUs and cause timeouts.

Proposed Redwood Dedicated configuration (initial recommendation)
- Reserved capacity: 8x A100-equivalent GPUs (reserved), single-tenant pool for Orion Health.
- Scaling plan: baseline of 6 GPUs for steady-state with 2 reserved burst nodes to handle scheduled batch windows; autoscale policy to add ephemeral nodes up to 12 for >90th percentile burst events.
- Isolation: VPC peering plus dedicated subnets; optional on-prem connector for air-gapped data pulls.
- SLAs & targets: 99.95% monthly uptime for Dedicated control plane; 95th/99th and p95 latency target for short inference calls set to 120ms (we’ll instrument tracing during pilot).

Next steps / asks
1) I’ll share a draft SOW and a pricing proposal (attached) by EOD today.  
2) Please confirm the primary procurement contact and target PO date — you mentioned procurement kick-off the week of 6/15.
3) Can you confirm compliance requirements beyond SOC2 (e.g., specific retention windows, encryption-at-rest keys)? If you want, we can loop in Security for a short call.

Attachments: Redwood_Dedicated_Proposal_ORION_v1.pdf (pricing + config), initial SOW template.

If that aligns, I’ll schedule a 30-minute technical run-through with Marcus and Rishi next week to finalize the config and capacity sizing.

Thanks —

Marissa Cole
Sr. Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0142

From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@orionhealth.com>

Date: Mon, 8 Jun 2026 08:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call recap — dedicated capacity needs & next steps

Thanks Marissa — this summary is perfect and covers everything we discussed. A few quick confirmations and questions:  

- Procurement timeline: we’re targeting a PO by the end of June (internal approvals dependent on final SOW and price).
- Primary procurement contact is Jordan Patel (cc’d) — he’ll own the PO and contract review.
- Compliance: SOC2 + HIPAA. We also need support for our KMS (AWS KMS) and audit log exports for quarterly audits.
- Capacity tweak: during peak processing windows we may need up to 14 GPUs for short bursts (about 2–3 hours per day). Can you confirm whether Redwood Dedicated can support a burst limit to 14 and how billing/commit would be structured for that usage pattern?

Request: Please send the SOW + indicative pricing and any security questionnaire answers we can share with Procurement. If possible, scheduling the technical follow-up for Wed 6/10 or Thu 6/11 in the morning PT would work for our infra team.

Appreciate it —

Samantha Lee
